node.title: Re^2: File::Temp survival and scope created by "do"
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Interesting...

So somehow [doc://do] blocks aren't blocks either?

I'm pretty sure a [doc://do] BLOCK has its own lexical scope:

$ perl -wMstrict -le 'my $x="A"; do { print $x; my $x="B"; print $x }; print $x' A B A $ perl -wMstrict -le 'do { my $x="A" }; print $x' Global symbol "$x" requires explicit package name (did you forget to declare "my $x"?) at -e line 1. Execution of -e aborted due to compilation errors.

But it seems to me like this might have something to do with a [doc://do] block being able to return a value:

$ perl -wMstrict -le 'sub Foo::DESTROY {print "BLAM"}; print "A"; do { my $x = bless {}, "Foo" }; print "B"' A B BLAM $ perl -wMstrict -le 'sub Foo::DESTROY {print "BLAM"}; print "A"; do { my $x = bless {}, "Foo"; 1 }; print "B"' A BLAM B

Although I don't know why do { my $x = bless {}, "Foo" } vs. do { bless {}, "Foo" } makes a difference either. Seems strange to me.
